findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite AC-2/guard to scope the constant grep to the comment-limit lineage (e.g. only the suffix literal and the outbound comment/adf limit constants), because 32767 legitimately appears in runtime.py, _config_schema.py, jira_datacenter/settings.py and backend.py prose under src/rebar/_engine.
evidence: search '32767' hits: _config_schema.py:506, runtime.py:46 (both under src/rebar), jira_datacenter/backend.py:244-257 (prose), jira_datacenter/settings.py:60/64, jira/comment_limits.py:41, jira_family/rich_text.py:60
runtime.py:46 _DEFAULT_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767 is under src/rebar/_engine and unrelated to the comment-suffix consolidation
findings.finding: AC-2 asserts 'grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar/_engine returns one file', but 32767 appears in at least six files under src/rebar/_engine: adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:41, adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:60, adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py (prose, ~244-257), adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:60/64, plus 32767 in runtime.py:46 and _config_schema.py:506 (these last two are outside _engine? no — runtime.py IS under _engine). Even after consolidation, jira_datacenter/settings.py, jira_datacenter/backend.py prose, and runtime.py legitimately hold 32767, so the grep cannot return one file.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar/_engine returns one file'
scenarios: The guard/AC grep is run and returns multiple files (runtime default, DC settings default-value, DC backend primary-source prose), failing the AC even when the consolidation is done correctly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the mutation-enactment consumer (dispatch_one.py:371-379, `_record_comment_id`/add_comment call) in Scope and state how the mutation's new `wire_body` reaches `add_comment` now that fit/encode leave the adapter.
evidence: dispatch_one.py:371-379: `body = entry.get("body", "")` then `client.add_comment(jira_key, body)`
outbound_comments.py:601-606 builds the mutation dict `{action:add, body:_decorate_outbound_comment(body), local_comment_key}` — plan changes this to carry wire_body
Scope lists acli_cli_ops.py and the two backend.py but not dispatch_one.py
findings.finding: The mutation-enactment consumer that reads the outbound comment mutation dict and calls add_comment is not enumerated in Scope. dispatch_one.py:371-379 reads entry.get('body') and calls add_comment(jira_key, body); the plan makes 'the mutation carry wire_body' and 'add_comment only encode and send', which shifts fit/decorate/encode out of add_comment into mutation construction and changes what the enactment site must pass.
findings.location: Approach ('the mutation carries wire_body; Cloud and DC add_comment only encode and send') / Scope
scenarios: A comment is added: the enactment site passes the old plain-text body to add_comment, but add_comment now assumes it receives (or no longer produces) the wire body — mismatch or double/absent encoding.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether `fit_comment_as_sent` is retained (as `fit_for_send(...).landed_text`) or replaced, and enumerate the fit_comment Protocol in `_backend.py` plus both backend `fit_comment` implementers as consumers to reconcile.
evidence: _backend.py:486 references `outbound_comments.fit_comment_as_sent` in the fit_comment Protocol docstring
backend.py:176-178 and jira_datacenter/backend.py:314-316 both `from rebar_reconciler.outbound_comments import fit_comment_as_sent` and return it from fit_comment
Scope omits _backend.py
findings.finding: The Backend-port fit_comment contract and its callers are consumers of the renamed composition but only partly enumerated. _backend.py:481-493 documents fit_comment as 'must return exactly the marker-free body the backend's SEND path lands (see outbound_comments.fit_comment_as_sent)'; the plan renames that composition to fit_for_send returning FittedComment(landed_text, wire_body). _backend.py is not in Scope, and Cloud's sanitizer.fit_comment (backend.py:154-178) and DC's fit_comment (jira_datacenter/backend.py:303-316) delegate to fit_comment_as_sent and would need their return-contract reconciled with the new struct-returning function.
findings.location: Approach ('Add fit_for_send ... The differ keys on landed_text') / Scope
scenarios: fit_for_send returns a FittedComment struct, but the fit_comment port contract and its two implementers still expect/return a bare str landed body; the differ key vs. port contract diverge.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that add_comment stops fitting/re-encoding independently, how wire_body is threaded to the mutation, and that the send uses the same codec (or wire_body) that fit_for_send used, so the key and sent bytes cannot drift.
evidence: acli_cli_ops.py:530 builds its own codec: AdfCodec(rich='cloud' in cutover_clients()) and fits at send time (line 531)
cutover_clients() is documented (rich_text.py:72-78) as read at CALL time, so a send-time codec can differ from a differ-time codec if the flag flips
SupportsComments.add_comment(remote_id, body: str) (backend.py:530) takes a str body; the plan does not describe how the pre-computed wire_body reaches it or that the internal fit is deleted
findings.finding: The plan says adapters 'only encode and send' but does not specify (a) that the existing independent fit calls in acli_cli_ops.add_comment:531, jira/backend.add_comment, and DC sanitize_comment are removed, (b) how wire_body is carried to add_comment through the mutation, nor (c) that the send-time codec must be the SAME instance/cutover read as the codec injected into fit_for_send — leaving open the very key-vs-wire drift the plan aims to eliminate.
findings.location: Approach ('wire_body = fit_preserving_marker(decorate(body), fit) computed once ... the mutation carries wire_body; Cloud and DC add_comment only encode and send')
scenarios: If add_comment still re-fits/re-encodes with a freshly-built codec, an over-length body is fit twice or encoded by a codec whose cutover read differs from fit_for_send's, so key (decode_inbound(to_wire(wire_body))) != sent bytes

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the 32767 limit inventory from the symbol graph (find_referencing_symbols on the limit constant plus a grep for `32767` as a string), then either add `runtime.py:46` and `_config_schema.py:506` to Scope or narrow AC-2 to exclude the config/runtime defaults that are intentionally left in place.
evidence: Plan: 'the truncation suffix literal lives in three places ... and the limit in four (32767 ×3 vs 32000 at adf.py:332)'

grep 32767 in src/rebar: `_config_schema.py:506: comment_max_chars: int = 32767` and `_engine/rebar_reconciler/runtime.py:46: _DEFAULT_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767` — neither counted in '×3' nor listed in Scope
AC line 'grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar/_engine returns one file' is falsified by runtime.py:46 which is under src/rebar/_engine
findings.finding: The limit-constant inventory ('the limit in four') is hand-enumerated and omits two live 32767 definitions: `_config_schema.py:506` (`comment_max_chars: int = 32767`) and `_engine/rebar_reconciler/runtime.py:46` (`_DEFAULT_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767`). runtime.py:46 lies inside the AC-2 grep scope `src/rebar/_engine`, so AC-2's 'returns one file' cannot pass unless runtime.py is also changed, yet runtime.py (and _config_schema.py) are absent from Scope.
findings.location: Context/Problem: 'the limit in four (32767 ×3 vs 32000 at adf.py:332)'; Acceptance Criteria: 'grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar/_engine returns one file'
scenarios: runtime.py:46 keeps `_DEFAULT_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS = 32767` inside src/rebar/_engine, so the AC-2 grep returns >1 file and the guard test fails at land time

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the canonical limit value (32767 or 32000) in the Approach and justify why adf.py's differing 32000 is safe to change (or preserve), so the consolidation is not a silent behavior shift.
evidence: Context: 'the limit in four (32767 ×3 vs 32000 at adf.py:332)'
Approach: 'One suffix and one limit constant in jira_family/rich_text.py; delete the copies'
No stated resolution of the 32767-vs-32000 discrepancy
findings.finding: Consolidating the length limit to a single constant forces a choice between the two values in play (32767 used in three places, 32000 at adf.py:332), which is a behavior change, but the plan does not state which value becomes canonical.
findings.location: Approach: 'One suffix and one limit constant ... delete the copies'
scenarios: If adf.py previously truncated at 32000 and now uses 32767, comment bodies between 32000 and 32767 chars change from truncated to full — a silent behavior shift
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence: 'The canonical limit is 32767 (Jira's ADF max); adf.py's 32000 was an under-count and is superseded — confirmed harmless because <reason>.'

evidence: verify command `grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar/_engine` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify in Approach that only the SUFFIX literal is a true duplicate to unify; keep `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32000, serialized-ADF budget) distinct from the 32767 plain-char cap, and reconcile the `grep 32767|32000 returns one file` guard with these being legitimately separate constants.
evidence: adf.py:326-332: `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT: int = 32000` is a SERIALIZED-ADF budget ('a 32,767-char description observed serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars'; 'Target a budget safely under Jira's 32,767-char limit') — a different UNIT, not a copy of the plain-char cap.

jira_datacenter/backend.py:252-254: 'Cloud needs its own adapters/jira/comment_limits module not because its numbers differ but because its UNITS do — Cloud descriptions are limited in ADF-SERIALIZED size, and DC has no ADF inflation to measure.'
The suffix literal IS genuinely duplicated (3 byte-identical copies at comment_limits.py:46, adf.py:333, rich_text.py:69) — that consolidation is sound; the finding is about the LIMIT only.
findings.finding: The plan's limit consolidation ('One suffix and one limit constant in rich_text.py; delete the copies') conflates three semantically distinct numeric constants into one, treating them as accidental duplication when the codebase documents them as deliberately different.
findings.location: Approach section / AC line 'grep -rn "32767\|32000" returns one file'
scenarios: Merging 32000 and 32767 into one constant would either over-truncate Cloud comments (if 32000 wins) or over-run the ADF-serialized description budget (if 32767 wins).
The guard `grep returns one file` would force removing the 32000 literal even though it measures a different quantity than 32767.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize the adapter path prefixes (Context/Scope use 'adapters/...' shorthand while AC-2 uses 'src/rebar/_engine'); confirm all cited files resolve under src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/.

comment_limits.py:46 _TRUNCATION_SUFFIX, adf.py:333 _ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX, rich_text.py:69 _WIKI_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX all confirmed at the cited line numbers under the _engine/rebar_reconciler prefix
findings.finding: The Context cites the truncation-suffix and limit locations as 'adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:46', 'adf.py:333', 'jira_family/rich_text.py:69' and Scope lists paths like 'adapters/jira/backend.py'; the real tree roots these under src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/. findings.suggested_fix: Change AC2 to `grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar returns one file` (matching the Approach guard), or grep the specific adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py home.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'one limit constant' claim with the existing 049e config-resolved `comment_max_chars` (config default 32767, admin-settable) so the consolidation does not remove or duplicate the existing config surface.
evidence: _config_schema.py:506 + comment: `comment_max_chars: int = 32767` is admin-settable, 'Env override REBAR_RECONCILER_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS is auto-derived'.

jira_datacenter/backend.py:256-263 (bug 049e): 'that property is ADMIN-SETTABLE ... 32767 is only the DEFAULT. It now comes from [tool.rebar.reconciler].comment_max_chars ... Resolution is LAZY ... and cached'.
The plan's own Testing already says 'DC bodies fit at comment_max_chars()', acknowledging DC resolves a ceiling rather than a literal — so the 'one limit constant' framing is internally in tension.
findings.finding: The plan asserts DC's limit is a literal to consolidate into rich_text.py, but DC's comment ceiling is already an admin-settable config value resolved at runtime, not a hard constant — consolidating it away risks losing the existing config surface.
findings.location: Approach 'one limit constant in jira_family/rich_text.py; delete the copies' vs Testing 'DC bodies fit at comment_max_chars()'
scenarios: A guard that forces the DC 32767 literal to move into rich_text.py would collide with the config-resolved ceiling, since `comment_max_chars()` reads config, not a module constant.

findings.finding: The Context claims 'the key-side codec.normalize_outbound(...) at outbound_comments.py:572 is still an unmatched extra step', but the current differ key path does not call codec.normalize_outbound at all: lines 591-592 build the compare key as _normalize_comment_body(codec.to_wire(_decorate_outbound_comment(sanitizer.fit_comment(body)))), and line 583 explicitly describes normalize_outbound routing as 'the previous shape' (already replaced). Line 572 is an emersed-specific-mutt comment, not a normalize_outbound call.
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'the key-side codec.normalize_outbound(...) at outbound_comments.py:572 is still an unmatched extra step'
scenarios: The motivating 'unmatched extra step' the story sets out to remove may not exist on the current key path, weakening the problem statement and the diff the author expects to write.
